key_insight: Benchmarking 20 GWAS–scRNA-seq mapping methods showed that CATCH, a Cauchy-combination approach, was the most robust overall for identifying trait-associated cell types.
clinical_relevance: This work helps researchers prioritize the most relevant cell types for disease traits, improving biological interpretation of genetic findings and guiding downstream functional studies.
method: Compared two major strategies: "single cell to GWAS" and "GWAS to single cell".
Used PubMed evidence plus LLM-assisted literature synthesis to build a literature-informed benchmark.
Evaluated performance using simulations and real-data benchmarks across multiple trait-cell type mapping methods.
evidence_signal: The benchmark integrated published evidence and assessed 20 methods, finding that CATCH consistently balanced high statistical power with strong false-positive control.
watch_item: Method performance depends on factors like cell-type specificity metrics, GWAS power, and the breadth of scRNA-seq reference datasets, so results may vary by dataset and trait.
paper_title: Benchmarking methods integrating GWAS and single-cell transcriptomic data for mapping trait-cell type associations
